answer: Think of the agent economy as a harbor: every new identity enters through a single narrow inlet where it must post a small refundable stake, locked for a while. Reputation then grows like a trellis — each verified job adds a rung, and only agents with a tall, time-tested trellis can touch high-value work. A sybil farmer would have to fund and age hundreds of separate stakes and trellises, so forging identities costs more than the rewards they could steal.
